# Parameters

Scene parameters for the interactive player and exports.

**Contents:**

- [`k.Int`](#k-int): Integer scene parameter in the range `[lo, hi]`: `k.Int(3, 12, default=5)`.
- [`k.Float`](#k-float): Real-valued scene parameter in the range `[lo, hi]`: `k.Float(0.5, 2, default=1)`.
- [`k.Bool`](#k-bool): Boolean scene parameter: `k.Bool(default=True)`.
- [`k.Choice`](#k-choice): Scene parameter with fixed options: `k.Choice([k.BLUE, k.RED])` (the default is the first option, or `default=`).
- [`k.Str`](#k-str): Text scene parameter: `k.Str(default="...")`.

Back to the [reference index](README.md).

<a id="k-int"></a>
### `k.Int` *(class)*

```python
k.Int(lo: int, hi: int, default: int | None = None)
```

Integer scene parameter in the range `[lo, hi]`: `k.Int(3, 12, default=5)`. Parameters reach the scene function as signals: in video they take the `default` (or `--param name=value` on the CLI) and in interactive output they become controls. Reading a parameter with `.now` freezes it at build time (lint W1301).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lo` | `int` | required |   |
| `hi` | `int` | required |   |
| `default` | `int \| None` | `None` | Integer scene parameter in the range `[lo, hi]`: `k.Int(3, 12, default=5)`. |

**Example:**

```python
@k.scene(params={"n": k.Int(1, 10, default=3)})
def count(s: k.Scene, n: k.Signal[int]):
    label = k.Text(lambda: f"n = {n():.0f}", size=0.9).place(at="center")
    s.play(k.write(label))
```

**See also:** [`k.Float`](#k-float), [`k.scene`](scene.md#k-scene).

**Members:**

- [`validate`](#int-validate): Check a value given on the command line (`--param`) against the range.


<a id="k-float"></a>
### `k.Float` *(class)*

```python
k.Float(lo: float, hi: float, default: float | None = None)
```

Real-valued scene parameter in the range `[lo, hi]`: `k.Float(0.5, 2, default=1)`. Parameters reach the scene function as signals: in video they take the `default` (or `--param name=value` on the CLI) and in interactive output they become controls. Reading a parameter with `.now` freezes it at build time (lint W1301).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lo` | `float` | required |   |
| `hi` | `float` | required |   |
| `default` | `float \| None` | `None` | Real-valued scene parameter in the range `[lo, hi]`: `k.Float(0.5, 2, default=1)`. |

**Example:**

```python
@k.scene(params={"r": k.Float(0.5, 3, default=1.5)})
def radius(s: k.Scene, r: k.Signal[float]):
    c = k.Circle(r=r).place(at="center")
    s.play(k.draw(c))
```

<a id="k-bool"></a>
### `k.Bool` *(class)*

```python
k.Bool(default: bool = False)
```

Boolean scene parameter: `k.Bool(default=True)`. Parameters reach the scene function as signals: in video they take the `default` (or `--param name=value` on the CLI) and in interactive output they become controls. Reading a parameter with `.now` freezes it at build time (lint W1301).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | `bool` | `False` | Boolean scene parameter: `k.Bool(default=True)`. |

**Example:**

```python
@k.scene(params={"grid": k.Bool(default=True)})
def with_grid(s: k.Scene, grid: k.Signal[bool]):
    ax = k.Axes(x=(0, 5, 1), y=(0, 3, 1)).place(at="center")
    tag = k.Text("grid on", visible=grid).place(above=ax, gap=0.3)
    s.play(k.draw(ax), k.fade_in(tag))
```

**See also:** [`k.Choice`](#k-choice), [`k.scene`](scene.md#k-scene).

**Members:**

- [`validate`](#bool-validate): Accept booleans and `true/false/yes/no/on/off/1/0` from the command line.

<a id="k-choice"></a>
### `k.Choice` *(class)*

```python
k.Choice(options: Sequence[Any], default: Any = None)
```

Scene parameter with fixed options: `k.Choice([k.BLUE, k.RED])` (the default is the first option, or `default=`). Parameters reach the scene function as signals: in video they take the `default` (or `--param name=value` on the CLI) and in interactive output they become controls. Reading a parameter with `.now` freezes it at build time (lint W1301).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `Sequence[Any]` | required |   |
| `default` | `Any` | `None` | Scene parameter with fixed options: `k.Choice([k.BLUE, k.RED])` (the default is the first option, or `default=`). |

**Example:**

```python
@k.scene(params={"color": k.Choice([k.BLUE, k.RED], default=k.RED)})
def choice(s: k.Scene, color: k.Signal[k.Color]):
    sq = k.Square(2, fill=color, fill_opacity=0.6).place(at="center")
    s.play(k.draw(sq))
```

**See also:** [`k.Int`](#k-int), [`k.scene`](scene.md#k-scene).

**Members:**

- [`validate`](#choice-validate): Check that a value given on the command line is one of the options.


<a id="k-str"></a>
### `k.Str` *(class)*

```python
k.Str(default: str = "")
```

Text scene parameter: `k.Str(default="...")`. (`k.Text` is the text object; one name per concept.) Parameters reach the scene function as signals: in video they take the `default` (or `--param name=value` on the CLI) and in interactive output they become controls. Reading a parameter with `.now` freezes it at build time (lint W1301).

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | `str` | `""` | Text scene parameter: `k.Str(default="...")`. |

**Example:**

```python
@k.scene(params={"heading": k.Str(default="Hello")})
def greeting(s: k.Scene, heading: k.Signal[str]):
    title = k.Text(heading, size=0.9).place(at="center")
    s.play(k.write(title))
```

**See also:** [`k.Text`](text.md#k-text), [`k.scene`](scene.md#k-scene).

**Members:**

- [`validate`](#str-validate): Check a value given on the command line (`--param`).
